subject: science
verifiedAgainst: NCERT textbook listing (ncert.nic.in/textbook.php) + table of contents in the book prelims PDF

chapters.title: Exploring the Investigative World of Science

topics.title: Investigating like a scientist
outcomes: Learner can plan an investigation with variables, controls and repeated trials
misconceptions: Believes one experiment is enough to prove something
hooks: Which mask material blocks the most dust? test with a torch and cloth samples

topics.title: From data to conclusions
outcomes: Learner can organise results in tables and graphs and draw a conclusion supported by the evidence
misconceptions: Thinks that if two things happen together, one must cause the other
hooks: Do students who sleep more score better? collect class data

chapters.title: The Invisible Living World: Beyond Our Naked Eye

topics.title: Cells and their variety
outcomes: Learner can describe the cell as the basic unit of life and relate cell shapes to their functions
misconceptions: Thinks all cells look the same
Believes cells are found only in animals
hooks: Onion peel under a microscope; nerve cells are long

topics.title: Levels of organisation
outcomes: Learner can describe the levels cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism
misconceptions: Thinks organs are made directly of organisms
hooks: The heart is an organ, blood vessels a system

topics.title: Microorganisms and their roles
outcomes: Learner can identify kinds of microorganisms and their useful and harmful roles
misconceptions: Believes all microorganisms cause disease
hooks: Idli batter fermenting; curd; composting

topics.title: What health means
outcomes: Learner can describe health as physical, mental and social well-being and list habits that support it
misconceptions: Thinks you are healthy if you are not sick
hooks: A day in the life of a healthy teenager

topics.title: Communicable and non-communicable diseases
outcomes: Learner can distinguish communicable and non-communicable diseases and how they spread or develop
misconceptions: Believes antibiotics cure viral fevers like the common cold
Thinks diabetes can be caught from someone
hooks: Dengue and stagnant water in coolers

topics.title: Prevention, vaccines and treatment
outcomes: Learner can explain how vaccines, hygiene and clean surroundings prevent disease
misconceptions: Believes vaccines make you sick with the disease
hooks: India’s polio-free journey

topics.title: Magnetic effect of current: electromagnets
outcomes: Learner can make an electromagnet and explain how its strength can be changed
misconceptions: Thinks a coil of wire is a magnet even without current
hooks: Electric bells and cranes at scrapyards

topics.title: Heating effect of current
outcomes: Learner can explain the heating effect and its uses and dangers (fuses, MCBs)
misconceptions: Believes thicker wires heat up more
hooks: Electric iron, geyser and why wires catch fire when overloaded

topics.title: How batteries generate electricity
outcomes: Learner can make a simple voltaic cell (lemon cell) and compare dry and rechargeable batteries
misconceptions: Thinks a battery stores electric current like a tank
hooks: Lemon battery lighting an LED

topics.title: Force as push or pull and its effects
outcomes: Learner can describe effects of force on motion and shape
misconceptions: Believes a moving object needs a force to keep moving
Thinks a still object has no forces on it
hooks: Kicking a football; stopping a rolling ball

topics.title: Contact and non-contact forces
outcomes: Learner can classify forces such as muscular, friction, magnetic, electrostatic and gravitational
misconceptions: Thinks friction is always harmful
Believes gravity acts only on falling objects
hooks: Why a ball rolling on grass stops sooner than on a cement floor

topics.title: Weight and floating
outcomes: Learner can distinguish mass and weight and explain floating and sinking using upthrust
misconceptions: Thinks mass and weight are the same
Believes heavy objects always sink
hooks: A mug feels lighter under water in a bucket

topics.title: Pressure and air pressure
outcomes: Learner can explain pressure as force per area and show that air exerts pressure
misconceptions: Thinks air has no weight or pressure
hooks: Why a knife cuts and a school bag has wide straps; sucking juice with a straw

topics.title: Formation of winds
outcomes: Learner can explain how uneven heating causes pressure differences and wind
misconceptions: Believes wind blows from low to high pressure
hooks: Monsoon winds arriving in Kerala

topics.title: Thunderstorms, lightning and cyclones
outcomes: Learner can describe how cyclones form and list safety measures during storms and lightning
misconceptions: Thinks it is safe to stand under a tall tree during lightning
hooks: Cyclone warnings by IMD for Odisha

topics.title: Matter is made of particles
outcomes: Learner can give evidence that matter is made of tiny particles with spaces between them
misconceptions: Thinks particles of a substance expand or melt when heated (rather than move faster and spread)
Believes there is air between particles
hooks: Smell of agarbatti spreading; sugar dissolving in water

topics.title: States of matter and particle arrangement
outcomes: Learner can explain properties of solids, liquids and gases in terms of particle arrangement and motion
misconceptions: Believes particles in a solid do not move at all
Thinks gases have no mass
hooks: Why a gas fills a balloon but a solid keeps its shape

chapters.title: Nature of Matter: Elements, Compounds, and Mixtures

topics.title: Mixtures and their types
outcomes: Learner can identify mixtures (including air) and classify them as homogeneous or heterogeneous
misconceptions: Thinks air is a single substance
hooks: Sherbet vs bhel puri

topics.title: Pure substances: elements and compounds
outcomes: Learner can distinguish elements and compounds and give examples
misconceptions: Believes a compound keeps the properties of its elements
hooks: Water is not like hydrogen or oxygen at all

topics.title: Minerals
outcomes: Learner can explain what minerals are and why they are important
misconceptions: Thinks minerals are only found in medicines
hooks: Mica, bauxite and iron ore from Jharkhand and Odisha

chapters.title: The Amazing World of Solutes, Solvents, and Solutions

topics.title: Solutes, solvents and saturated solutions
outcomes: Learner can prepare a saturated solution and explain solubility
misconceptions: Thinks sugar disappears when it dissolves
Believes you can dissolve unlimited salt in water
hooks: Making nimbu-paani: how much sugar will dissolve?

topics.title: Effect of temperature on solubility; gases in water
outcomes: Learner can investigate how temperature affects solubility of solids and gases
misconceptions: Thinks gases do not dissolve in water
hooks: Fish need dissolved oxygen; soda goes flat when warm

topics.title: Density
outcomes: Learner can determine density and explain floating using density
misconceptions: Believes bigger objects are always denser
hooks: Why oil floats on water in a tadka

topics.title: Spherical mirrors and the laws of reflection
outcomes: Learner can state the laws of reflection and describe images formed by concave and convex mirrors
misconceptions: Thinks the angle of reflection is measured from the mirror surface
hooks: Rear-view mirrors are convex; dentist’s mirror is concave

topics.title: Lenses
outcomes: Learner can describe convex and concave lenses and the images they form
misconceptions: Believes a lens and a mirror form images in the same way
hooks: A magnifying glass burning paper in sunlight

topics.title: Phases of the Moon
outcomes: Learner can explain the phases of the Moon using the Sun-Earth-Moon positions
misconceptions: Thinks the Earth’s shadow causes the Moon’s phases
hooks: Track the Moon for a month; Karva Chauth and Eid moon sightings

topics.title: Lunar, solar and luni-solar calendars
outcomes: Learner can compare lunar, solar and luni-solar calendars and the Indian National Calendar
misconceptions: Believes all calendars have the same number of days
hooks: Why Diwali falls on a different date each year

topics.title: Ecosystems and food webs
outcomes: Learner can describe producers, consumers and decomposers and draw food chains and webs
misconceptions: Thinks the arrows in a food chain point to the eater’s food rather than the flow of energy
Believes removing one organism will not affect others
hooks: A pond ecosystem near your village

topics.title: Human-made ecosystems and farms
outcomes: Learner can explain how healthy ecosystems support farms and how human-made ecosystems work
misconceptions: Thinks a farm is not an ecosystem
hooks: Bees and pollination in mustard fields

chapters.title: Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet

topics.title: What makes Earth suitable for life
outcomes: Learner can explain how Earth’s position, size, atmosphere and magnetic field support life
misconceptions: Thinks other planets in the solar system can support life like Earth
hooks: Why Mars is cold and Venus is very hot

topics.title: Balance among air, water, soil and living things
outcomes: Learner can describe how resources and living things interact and why balance matters
misconceptions: Believes nature can absorb any amount of pollution
hooks: The ozone layer and sunscreen

topics.title: Continuity of life: asexual and sexual reproduction
outcomes: Learner can distinguish asexual and sexual reproduction with examples
misconceptions: Thinks only animals reproduce
hooks: Growing a money plant from a cutting
